name: Pennsylvania
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Pennsylvania's only alternate base year is for a work-related injury.

dependentAllowances.note: $5 a week for a dependent spouse, or a first dependent child if there is no spouse, and $3 for one more child; each must be wholly or chiefly supported by you.

duration.creditWeeksMean: A credit week is any week of the base period in which you earned $116 or more.

notModeled: The other route to a weekly rate: half your full-time weekly wage, where that is higher than the table's.
A credit week is a week you earned $116 or more; count them from your pay stubs.

citation.sourceDocument: PA L&I, UC eligibility and the §404(e) rate table; 56 Pa.B. 448 (Jan. 17, 2026); UC benefit guide and rate FAQs
citation.sourceNote: The table L&I publishes runs from $1,688-$1,712 of high-quarter wages at $68 to "15,388 or more" at $605, in $25 rows. All 548 rows were checked on 2026-10-19 against a closed form: row = (high quarter - 1,688) / 25 rounded down, rate = 98% of (69 + row) rounded up, the 98% being Act 144's 2% reduction, which is why eleven rates appear on two rows; and each row's qualifying wages (Part C) = (row start + 24) / 0.63 rounded up. Short of Part C, the rate steps down to either of the next two rows (§404(a)(3)). "Not less than thirty-seven per centum (37%)" of base-year wages must be outside the high quarter (§401(a)(2)). Weeks are credit weeks, "any calendar week ... in which an individual earned $116 or more", from 18 to 26. 56 Pa.B. 448: "the maximum weekly benefit rate for calendar year 2026 will remain at $605." L&I's FAQ: payments are "reduced by 3.2 percent beginning with the week ending January 7, 2023", so a $605 rate pays $585. The dependent allowance is $5 and $3, at most $8 (benefit guide).
